title: High-speed atomic force microscopy of membrane proteins: From dynamic imaging to integrative structural biology.
authors: Shin, Eunji; Mount, Jonathan; Scheuring, Simon
one_liner_zh: 该文综述高速原子力显微镜对膜蛋白动态成像及与MD模拟等整合的结构生物学应用，涉及蛋白质结构动态但以实验技术为主，计算建模仅作为辅助整合手段。
abstract: High-speed atomic force microscopy (HS-AFM) enables direct, label-free visualization of membrane proteins in lipid bilayers with nanometer spatial resolution and millisecond temporal resolution. Recent studies revealed transient conformational states, dynamic oligomerization changes, and membrane-mediated organization of membrane proteins that are not readily captured by conventional structural or biophysical approaches. Advances in experimental design-including membrane reconstitution strategies, stimulus-coupled imaging, high-temporal-resolution acquisition, and computational reconstruction-have further expanded the scope of HS-AFM. When integrated with complementary techniques such as cryo-electron microscopy, molecular dynamics simulations, and single-molecule methods, HS-AFM provides a powerful and versatile tool for linking membrane protein structure, dynamics, and function in native-like environments.
abstract_zh: 高速原子力显微镜（HS-AFM）能够直接、无标记地可视化脂质双分子层中的膜蛋白，具备纳米级空间分辨率和毫秒级时间分辨率。近期研究揭示了膜蛋白的瞬态构象状态、动态寡聚化变化及膜介导的组织结构，这些现象难以通过传统结构或生物物理方法捕获。实验设计的进展——包括膜重构策略、刺激耦合成像、高时间分辨率采集及计算重建——进一步拓展了HS-AFM的应用范围。当与冷冻电子显微镜、分子动力学模拟及单分子方法等互补技术整合时，HS-AFM为在类天然环境中连接膜蛋白结构、动力学与功能提供了强大且多功能的工具。
